text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs expects no essential change in Hungarian-British relations following the Labour Party victory in last Thursday's UK elections.

- Viktor Orban, president of the Young Democrats, remarked on the weekend that diplomatic statements supportive of Hungary's accession to the EU should be treated with reservations, since the heads of the EU member countries are trying to put off disadvantageous decisions.

- The opposition parties will propose again today that Parliament set up investigating commissions, one to examine the properties founded by the Hungarian Socialist Workers' Party. The other proposal calls for an investigation of properties owned by the Democratic Forum and the Young Democrats.

- If farmers continue to withhold production data the cabinet can only guess at the amount of grain, milk, potatoes and meat produced in Hungary, and most subsidies will continue to land in the pockets of the unscrupulous, according to a senior Agriculture Ministry official.
- Gyula Kosa, president of the Agricultural Producers Advocacy Organization, (Metesz) the most militant farmers' group, has vowed to press ahead with more demonstrations.

- Those who were born in Hungary before May 9, 1945, who suffered from fascist inspired regulations due to their Jewish origin, and who live in this country today can apply to the Jewish Public Foundation in Hungary for life annuity.
- The presidium of the Christian Democrats will meet on Thursday to consider what steps to take to resolve the party's long-running leadership dispute.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told his Danish host Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen in Copenhagen Friday that Hungary would prefer to see the European Union honor the timetable for expansion agreed at the 1995 Madrid summit conference.
- Mortgage institutions may be able to start operations in the middle of May, as the review of their applications will soon be at an end.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The economic cabinet plans to cut Ft 3.5 billion from higher education in the 1998 budget, according to a plan drawn up by the Finance Ministry.
- The Defense Ministry Procurement Office has challenged the Ft 20 million fine imposed by the Public Procurement Council in a recent missile tender case.
- The motorway concession company Alfold Koncesszios Autopalya Rt. (AKA) will spend Ft 30 billion on extending the M5 motorway this year
NEPSZABADSAG
- About 20,000 Chinese live in Hungary illegally today, according to an official survey, and cost the state budget Ft 30 billion through illegal trade.
NEPSZAVA
- The Socialist Party has accepted the nomination of Matyas Eorsi, Free Democrat chairman of the foreign affairs committee, to the post of political state secretary for foreign affairs.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Budapest representative of the International Monetary Fund said a report on Hungary will be submitted to the IMF board of directors any day now.
